title: Identity and Access Management quick learning plan
principle: Begin with the access boundary and accountable subject, then add identity assurance, trust relationships, policy decisions, lifecycle governance, and the systems that enforce authentication.

fast.method: Read each summary and worked example, answer the recall checks aloud, and use the scenario seed to name the subject, evidence, policy decision, enforcement point, and revocation path.

standard.method: Complete every section, visual, recall check, and scenario seed. Revisit the same access request across physical, logical, federated, lifecycle, and authentication-system perspectives.

sessions: Day 1: redraw the access-control boundary and explain identification, authentication, authorization, and accounting without merging them.
Day 4: compare RBAC, ABAC, MAC, DAC, rule-based, and risk-based decisions for one high-impact data set; include the enforcement point.
Day 7: trace a workforce identity and a service identity from proofing or registration through authentication, access review, incident revocation, and deprovisioning.

completionEvidence: Can distinguish physical access, logical access, identification, authentication, authorization, and accounting.
Can select identity proofing, authenticator, federation, and session controls that match consequence and trust boundaries.
Can explain why an authorization model and an authentication protocol solve different problems.
Can detect privilege creep and describe an auditable joiner-mover-leaver or service-account lifecycle.
